I deleted Chrome and went back to Firefox exclusively a while back - I concur entirely. That said it's irritating how frequently firefox updates these days. I block about a hundred sites in my hosts file. I generally don't block advertising, but I block Google ads. They have too much power and too much control over the market. I'd rather not block the smaller companies.

I'm not having crash problems with Firefox.

I agree that Firefox updates too often. How urgent can all these upgrades be? I complained to them about it. I"m stickin' with Firefox!

I recommend ghostery extension or a similar variant - many sites have 10-15 trackers that it will block. Another setting I advise is "delete history and cookies" at shutdown. So each time you close Firefox to update or resolve a crash haha, or just to clear RAM, it will dump most of the stuff you've picked up in that session. The key is to make yourself hard to track. Never "verify with your phone number" and try to use multiple email addresses for various purposes.

as for advertising I think we very much need to move away from the ad-supported concept. Web publishing will eventually benefit from a micropayments type service. Most services like email, etc, we can and should pay for, as long as the price is reasonable. By blocking ads you help ruin the marketplace for ads which will promote new revenue generation models. The density of corporate america on this issues is hard to fathom - newspapers are the worst. Some of the dogshit they're peddling is so bad it's shocking they have the nerve to try and charge subscription fees. Newsflash: you can't outsource your newsroom to some sweatshop that generates half-ass, two paragraph glorified tweets and expect anyone to pay for it. And if you want to charge for content you need to give the users a sample: give us your credit card, use it free entirely for a month. Then you have to CHOOSE to pay after that, no auto-enrollment. Once users see your product and get used to using it they will likely pay the nominal fee to continue to have access, provided it's not shit.
